text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure usually has no signs or symptoms, which is why it is often called the "silent killer".

list.snippet: No warning signs: Most people with high blood pressure feel completely fine.
Years of damage: The condition can quietly harm your heart, brain, and kidneys without you knowing.
Testing is essential: The only way to know your numbers is to get a blood pressure check. You can learn more from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text_blocks.snippet: When blood pressure rises to dangerous levels—usually 180/120 mm Hg or higher—some people may notice warning signs.

list.snippet: Headaches: A severe, sudden, or unusual headache.
Vision changes: Sudden blurry vision or other eyesight problems.
Breathing issues: Shortness of breath or difficulty catching your breath.
Chest pain: Tightness or pain in the chest area.
Neurological signs: Sudden confusion, dizziness, or stroke symptoms like facial drooping or weakness.

text_blocks.snippet: If your blood pressure is over 180/120 mm Hg and you have chest pain, shortness of breath, confusion, or weakness, call 911 immediately. You can read more about emergency signs on the American Heart Association site.
